title: Hard-slicing GPUs with tenant pause/resume and preemptive-noise throttling
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Scope: Implement a tenancy isolation mode that provides deterministic per-tenant throughput guarantees by combining hard GPU partitioning (hard-slices), a tenant pause/resume lifecycle, and a preemptive noise-throttle layer. This ticket covers runtime kernel changes, scheduler controls, autoscaler interactions, operational runbooks, and required observability.

Goals:
- Provide a 'hard-slice' option customers can enable on Dedicated pools that reserves fixed GPU lanes (MIG or CUDA SM allocation) to achieve firm throughput guarantees.
- Add a lightweight tenant pause/resume API to evacuate a tenant's jobs from a node for maintenance or rebalancing without losing reservations.
- Implement a preemptive-noise throttler that detects emergent noisy-neighbor behavior (kernel-level tail latency or sustained SM/PCIe saturation) and applies graduated throttles before eviction.

Out of scope: full scheduler rewrite, multi-region routing, and customer billing changes (billing work tracked separately).

Acceptance criteria:
- New hard-slice allocation mode can be toggled per-dedicated-pool and produces predictable throughput with less than 10% variance under normal load in synthetic benchmarks.
- Pause/resume API can successfully drain and restore up to 200 tenants during scheduled maintenance with <2m median downtime per tenant.
- Preemptive-noise throttler reduces noisy-kernel-induced tail latency by at least 40% in chaos tests and emits actionable alerts.
- End-to-end test coverage + benchmark dashboard published and smoke rollout to a staging Dedicated cluster.
comments: 2026-01-18 - Asha Mehta: Created ticket after architecture review. Key constraint: must interoperate with autoscaler to avoid double-counting capacity. Linked design intent doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Hard+Slice+Proposal

2026-01-25 - Diego Alvarez: Spike complete. Verified MIG and CUDA-based soft partitioning both viable; MIG gives stronger isolation but requires GPU families with MIG support. Decision: support both but default to MIG when available. Spike notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/hnf-hard-slice-spike

2026-02-02 - Priya Kaur (SRE): Observability checklist added. We need per-tenant SM utilization, kernel latency histogram, and pause/resume event traces. Created dashboard template: infra.logs/dashboards/tenant-isolation-v1

2026-02-15 - Diego Alvarez: Implementation started. Runtime changes: new allocation path (AllocMode=HARD_SLICE) + tenant lifecycle handlers. Introduced 'eviction-safety' window to coordinate with autoscaler. Local branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/feature/hard-slice

2026-02-23 - QA (E. Nguyen): Integration test plan uploaded. Tests: 1) steady-state throughput with 10 tenants; 2) noisy neighbor injection via microbench tool; 3) pause/resume storm (200 tenants). Test plan: https://docs.google.com/document/d/Isolation-Test-Plan

2026-02-28 - Design (Maya Patel): UX copy for Console pause/resume modal. Added confirmation flows and tenant-level SLA warning if pause will drop below guaranteed throughput. UI mock: https://figma.com/file/console-pause-resume

2026-03-03 - Diego Alvarez: Implemented preemptive-noise throttler. Algorithm: monitor rolling 30s P99 kernel time + SM occupancy; if exceed threshold, reduce new request admission by graded throttle (25/50/75) before triggering eviction. Rationale: prefer throttling to preserve reservations and avoid hard evictions.

2026-03-07 - SRE (Priya Kaur): Added anomaly detector and PagerDuty rule: noise-throttle >=50% for 3 consecutive minutes -> SEV3. Eviction events remain SEV2. Config stored in runtime-config service under 'isolation.noise_throttle'.

2026-03-10 - Diego Alvarez: Performance notes from staging run: All MIG-backed clusters met throughput variance target (~7% median), CUDA-slice fallback showed higher variance (12-15%) under pathological kernel mixes. Plan: explicit warning for CUDA-slice customers and automated recommendation to use MIG GPUs when firm SLAs required.

2026-03-13 - Asha Mehta: Rollout plan approved. Phased deploy: 1) internal staging smoke; 2) invited customers (2 pilot tenants); 3) general availability to Dedicated customers. Rollback: disable AllocMode=HARD_SLICE and resume prior allocation strategy. Runbook and postmortem template linked: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Hard+Slice+Runbook
implementation_notes: Runtime: add AllocMode enum (SHARED, SOFT_LANE, HARD_SLICE). Hard-slice uses node-level reservation tables and enforces cgroup v3 limits when available. Pause/resume implemented as a two-phase drain (stop new admits + soft-kill long-running inference jobs after grace) then release reservation flags. Throttler: token-bucket adapting to observed kernel latency with backoff multipliers. Autoscaler: treat hard-slice reservations as committed capacity (do not scale down below sum(reservations) + safety margin).
test_results: staging-2026-03-09: MIG cluster steady-state throughput variance 7% (pass)
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal staging verify (1 week). Phase 2: pilot with 2 enterprise customers (2 weeks) under SRE supervision. Phase 3: GA to Dedicated pools toggled by admin. Feature flag: isolation.hard_slice.enabled. Monitoring and automated rollback in place.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hard-slices cause underutilization of GPU if reservations are conservative. Mitigation: autoscaler recommendation engine proposes right-sizing and supports overcommit windows for low-priority lanes.
Risk: Pause/resume may interact poorly with long-lived streaming connections. Mitigation: add per-connection drains and close-on-maintenance hooks in SDKs; document expected behaviors.
Risk: Customers on non-MIG hardware see worse SLAs. Mitigation: telemetry will surface recommended GPU families; Console will surface guidance during pool creation.
